assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation turns a small molecule into a programmable recognition-and-effector device, a molecular design principle that redefines what is druggable. Clear conceptual originality (heterobifunctional degraders) joined to the mechanistic discovery of molecular glues, with immediate use by clinicians and industry. The discovery changed what chemists and clinicians can actually do.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs and the first cell-active designs; Ciulli supplied structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex rationale. The cereblon/thalidomide glue mechanism (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray) is a parallel strand, so any three-person split leaves out deserving contributors.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades since the first PROTAC; many degraders are in clinical trials, and independent confirmation and broad adoption are clear. Clinical approval is still pending but the chemistry is firmly established, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation between the PROTAC strand and the thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue strand is unresolved.
Clinical benefit is not yet fully demonstrated, which could argue for waiting.
Credit among Sakamoto, Kim, Crews and Deshaies for the earliest PROTAC work is something I cannot verify independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs that add designed amino acids to proteins in living cells are a rare example of rational molecular design with precise control, now spanning biophysics, protein engineering, therapeutic proteins and biomaterials. Important, original and broadly enabling.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first general in vivo method and the early orthogonal pairs; Chin extended it to eukaryotes, quadruplet codons and genomically recoded organisms. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important pieces, which leaves some risk of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of use and extensive independent adoption, with an interpretation that is stable. Recognition is mature, and the field's continued growth supports timing.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama is unclear.
Medical translation (for example, protein therapeutics) is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Condensate formation by multivalent biomolecules reframed intracellular organisation, linking physical chemistry to cell function and disease. The conceptual impact is large and spans chemistry, biophysics and medicine, though the mechanistic chemistry is less tightly defined than for a discrete invention.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules; Rosen defined multivalent interaction-driven phase separation in vitro; Pappu and Mittag provided sequence-grammar theory. A three-person limit is difficult and some excluded contributors are central.
assessment.maturity: Highly cited and quickly adopted, but the physiological relevance of phase separation in cells is still debated and the interpretation is still evolving; the work may be somewhat premature for Chemistry.
uncertainties: Disputes over whether many condensates are physiologically relevant versus in vitro artefacts.
Fit to a chemistry prize rather than physiology or physics.
Priority and credit allocation among several equivalent contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a chemistry-driven delivery technology that made nucleic-acid medicines, including mRNA vaccines, practicable at scale. This is a clear example of molecular design with dramatic effect on what clinicians can do, and the impact is exceptional. Part of the discovery is formulation engineering rather than new chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues developed ionizable lipid LNP formulations and manufacturing; Anderson and Langer advanced lipid libraries and screening for potent delivery; Madden, Hope and MacLachlan contributed essential early steps. Attribution is complicated and overlaps with patent disputes.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale by approved vaccines and the siRNA drug patisiran, so confirmation is strong and recognition is timely, noting the 2023 Medicine prize already honored the mRNA modification side.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among the many LNP developers is contested.
Relation to the 2023 Medicine prize may count against it.
I am not certain which specific lipid innovations were decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors fuse programmable DNA recognition with a deaminase to make precise single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks, a new chemistry-informed tool with large biomedical consequences, including clinical trials. Highly original and broadly usable.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear intellectual leader; Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experimental work as trainees, and Nishida and Kondo reported a related approach. Considering the Crispr prize in 2020, a Liu-only configuration is possible, but this entry overlaps the prime-editing candidate.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely, with early clinical use, but the long-term therapeutic record is limited. Recognition may be somewhat early, and awarding the gene-editing area again so soon after 2020 is a consideration.
uncertainties: Overlap with prime editing (another candidate) and how credit would be partitioned.
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy are not yet established.
Whether the committee wishes to revisit genome editing after 2020.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single molecules electrically, combining protein engineering, chemistry of recognition and instrumentation, and it produced commercial long-read DNA sequencers and a general platform for single-molecule analysis. Strong, tangible impact on bioanalytical practice.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer showed the concept of DNA translocation; Bayley engineered protein pores and stochastic sensing; Akeson demonstrated controlled DNA motion enabling sequencing. Credit across several teams and the engineering-heavy commercial implementation is difficult to partition.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and confirmed independently over decades. The technology is mature, though the interpretation of fundamental contributions versus industrial development is a debate.
uncertainties: Fair split among the early concept, the engineered pore and the enzyme-controlled motion.
Part of the decisive work may be technology development outside academia.
I cannot verify current status of all credited individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed assembly of gold nanoparticles and spherical nucleic acids is a molecular-design platform that directly links biomolecular recognition to nanomaterial properties, and it underlies colorimetric detection, intracellular gene regulation and diagnostics. It is close to my own area, so I weight it with care, but the originality is clear.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin led the central discoveries with Storhoff, Mucic and Letsinger in the 1996 work; Alivisatos independently reported related DNA-nanocrystal assemblies, which creates some competing credit. A Mirkin-only configuration is cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent replication and many commercial diagnostic products, although the therapeutic impact of spherical nucleic acids is still being tested. Recognition is reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims with Alivisatos and others.
Clinical translation of SNAs is not yet established.
Possible bias because of my own work in related peptide-nanoparticle systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics lets researchers measure thousands of proteins and their modifications, transforming biological and clinical analysis. The impact is very large, with real clinical biomarker and systems-biology use, but the contribution is a cluster of methods rather than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the leading contributors to large-scale protein identification and quantitative workflows, with Gygi, Hunt and Heck also central. Three-laureate limit excludes important contributors, and credit overlaps with the native-MS candidate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, but part of the field was honored in 2002 (electrospray and MALDI), which may make a second MS prize less likely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a distinct discovery after the 2002 prize.
Division of credit among the many method developers.
Technical improvements may be viewed as incremental engineering.
